It's a load cell, but the certificate doesn't explicitly say "Analog load cell". I'll leave module_designation as null, and put "double ended shear beam load cell" in description.

- Fraction pLC (P_L): 0.7 → attribute `apportionment_factor_plc`, value 0.7 (converted from 0,7)
- Maximum capacity Emax: 4500 kg up to and including 22500 kg → range {min: 4500, max: 22500}, unit kg. Hmm — "up to and including 22500 kg". This is a range of capacities covered. Should this be a model matrix? It's expressed as a range, so keep as range value {min: 4500, max: 22500} with unit "kg". The instruction for R60 example converts comma-separated Emax values into a model matrix. Here it's "4500 kg up to and including 22500 kg" — a range. Could be interpreted as family of models. But per rule 2, ranges become {min, max}. I'll treat as type_level with range. Alternatively, model family with models Emax=4500kg ... 22500kg? The markdown doesn't enumerate variants, so type_level range is appropriate.
- Humidity Class: CH → value "CH", unit null
- Temperature range: -10 °C / +40 °C → {min: -10, max: 40}, unit °C
- Accuracy Class: D → value "D"
- Maximum number of load cell intervals n: 1000 → max_load_cell_intervals_nlc? The label "Maximum number of load cell intervals (n)" → canonical `max_load_cell_intervals_nlc` per example. Value 1000.
- Ratio Y = Emax/Vmin: 2250 → `ratio_y_emax_over_vmin`, value 2250
- Ratio Z = Emax/(2*DR): 1300 → `ratio_z_emax_over_dr`, value 1300

Model family: The cert covers a single type DSB1 with capacity range. Rule 4 says model family "include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant". The Emax range 4500–22500 kg could imply multiple variants but not explicitly enumerated. I'll not include model_family. Actually, hmm. R60 certs often cover a range. The example turned comma-list into models. Here it's a continuous range "4500 kg up to and including 22500 kg". I'll keep it as a type_level range characteristic since no discrete variants are enumerated. That seems most faithful.
